blocks.text: This page tracks the South Surrey and White Rock MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $996,000 for a typical home, down 5.4% over twelve months.
South Surrey and White Rock benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical South Surrey and White Rock home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $996,000 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.6% on the month, down 1.5% over three months, down 6.4% over six months and down 5.4% over the year. Over three years it is down 19.4%, and over five years down 12.9%.
The weakest one-year move in South Surrey and White Rock was for a townhouse homes at −9.2%; the strongest was an apartment at −3.5%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,606,500) and an apartment ($558,600) is $1,047,900, and a townhouse ($800,900) sits $242,300 above the apartment benchmark.

Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $860,000, South Surrey and White Rock is 15.8% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 6.4% against down 5.4% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, South Surrey and White Rock ranks 2 by all-home benchmark, with North Delta above it at $1,024,900 and Langley below it at $932,900.

Detached homes in South Surrey and White Rock: benchmark $1,606,500, little changed at −0.4% in a month, down 2.5% in three months, down 7.7% in six months, down 6.3% in a year, down 16.5% in three years and down 9.0% in five. That is 24.2% above the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,293,800).

Townhouse homes in South Surrey and White Rock: benchmark $800,900, little changed at +0.5% in a month, down 4.1% in three months, down 8.8% in six months, down 9.2% in a year, down 17.6% in three years and down 8.0% in five. That is 7.9% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($742,300).

Apartment homes in South Surrey and White Rock: benchmark $558,600, up 2.6% in a month, up 2.1% in three months, down 5.1% in six months, down 3.5% in a year, down 12.2% in three years and up 3.6% in five. That is 21.2% above the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($460,800).

blocks.text: Set against October 2025, South Surrey and White Rock had 54 detached sales (58 a year earlier), 35 townhouse sales (50 a year earlier) and 46 apartment sales (48 a year earlier). Month-end active listings were 559 detached (about 622 a year earlier), 261 townhouse (about 322 a year earlier) and 295 apartment (about 375 a year earlier). Dividing sales by active listings gives a sales-to-active ratio of 9.7% for detached, 13.4% for townhouse and 15.6% for apartment.

In dollars, the typical South Surrey and White Rock home is worth about $56,900 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,052,900. By type, detached homes lost about $108,000, from $1,714,500 to $1,606,500, townhouses lost about $81,100, from $882,000 to $800,900, and apartments lost about $20,300, from $578,900 to $558,600 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,064,100 six months ago and near $1,235,700 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $68,100 below the six-month mark and about $239,700 below the three-year mark. Against the Fraser Valley Board area, the South Surrey and White Rock benchmark is about $136,000 above the regional $860,000; a year earlier the difference was about $134,100 above.
South Surrey and White Rock sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 597 South Surrey and White Rock houses sold at a median of $1.67M (middle half $1.39M to $2.1M), half of them within 32 days. 529 condos sold at a median of $545,000 (middle half $480,000 to $670,000), half within 29 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.78M to $1.55M between November–January and August–October (114 and 127 sales).
